newsitem.title: JAPAN: Market confidence in euro needed at outset -- Gaddum.
newsitem.headline: Market confidence in euro needed at outset -- Gaddum.

text.p: It is necessary to develop the confidence of financial markets in the European single currency from the start of its launch, Bundesbank Vice-President Johann-Wilhelm Gaddum said on Tuesday.
"We must all be aware that the starting process is so that the market believes that they can develop confidence in this new currency. That is my point," he told a symposium in Tokyo.
Gaddum told the symposium on European economic and monetary union (EMU) that the criteria to describe the convergence is that it is necessary to start on the basis of creating confidence.
"The most important is that the starting group is so that they are successful. This is also in the interests of those entering later on," he said.

He made the comments during a panel discussion in which he had been asked to elaborate on his earlier remark that it would be no problem to launch EMU with a smaller number of countries if that provided stability.
He had said in a speech earlier: "There's nothing wrong with starting with a smaller range of participants if that makes it easier to launch a real community of stability."
The single European currency, the euro, is scheduled to be launched on January 1, 1999.
Gaddum said in his speech it is possible that not all European countries will join the EMU from its inception at the beginning of 1999.
